People come here for the calm, the authenticity and the lift queues that barely exist. Mallnitz – Ankogel's reputation as a family resort is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly, easygoing atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for getting children started on skiing. With a summit at 2636 m and a village at 1266 m, snow reliability at Mallnitz – Ankogel is generally dependable from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause tension early in the season, but conditions recover quickly once the first decent snowfalls arrive. A stay in Mallnitz – Ankogel is clearly on the expensive side: 54€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and high-altitude restaurants that are among the priciest in the Alps. It's the price of excellence, but it's worth being aware of it before you go. In short, Mallnitz – Ankogel doesn't compete with the giants of skiing and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest, often underrated destination that deserves to be (re)discovered.
